messages.author: 36e687535b49b809
messages.subject: GENEActiv .csv epoch file
parts:
Dear all,

Is possible to process .csv GENEactiv accelerometer file which was converted from .bin file with epoch period 60s, or GGIR can handle only .bin files? Because my script cant recognize .csv file in folder 

Thanks for response

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GENEActiv .csv epoch file
parts:
GGIR is designed to process raw data files, sample rate of typically more than 20 Hertz.
GGIR does not handle aggregated data like the one you are trying to process. Please use the .bin file instead.

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GENEActiv .csv epoch file
parts:
Hi Vincent,
Thanks for your amazing work!
You previously mentioned that raw data should be recorded more than 20 Hertz. And I know that if the raw data is too small, the programme may not recognize it.
Our raw data were all collected with a measurement frequency at 10 Hertz. I tried to .bin file and could generate results with GGIR (.csv can not, maybe it's relatively small).
I'm just wondering  if GGIR could analyze data collected at 10 Hertz and would the measurement frequency affect results?
Looking forward to your reply. Thank you very much!

Regards,
Laura

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GENEActiv .csv epoch file
parts:
Hi Laura,

Technically GGIR can handle data with a resolution as low as 3 Hertz, but from an interpretation perspective lower sample rates become more tricky. Follow the Nyquist-Shannon theorem a signal captures the frequencies below half its sample rate. So, a 10 Hertz recording captures frequencies below 5 Hertz. If you believe that frequencies above 5 hertz are either impossible or irrelevant for what you are trying to measure then no problem. However, if you have reason to believe otherwise then this could be an issue.
I guess is that magnitude of acceleration will be more strongly affected than sleep estimates. To be on the save side I generally recommend recording at higher sample rates.

Best,
Vincent
